There is no doubt that Tiffany Phan is one of the most talented Ultimate players out there. She joined the Ultimate family in 8th grade, and has since played with and against talented individuals from across the country. From her role as captain at Franklin High School, to representing team USA at U19 Junior Worlds in 2012 and 2014, to playing on Underground, the experience Tiff brings to any team is extensive. Tiff stands out on the field with her fierce handler motion and a face of determination that can instantly turn into the widest smile in the universe. Her first year at Western, she was on the USA Ultimate All-Freshman Northwest team. In her fourth and final year, Tiff has become a passionate leader and captain of Chaos. Tiffany is the role model the Ultimate community needs. She has dedicated her life to this sport, and has overcome physical, economic and racial barriers to get to where she stands now. Coming from a low-income community of color, Tiff has worked twice as hard to pay for school, build self-confidence, and give 110% at every practice. When Tiff tore her ACL and was out for the season, she still came to every game to support her teammates. She has actively built and maintained relationships with the Ultimate community, coaching and volunteering with youth programs in Seattle. Tiff is dedicated to making Ultimate accessible to all, and to empowering girls to believe in themselves. Tiffany may be the shortest person on Chaos, but we all look up to her. She has worked this season to not only make us better players, but better people. She approaches this sport with humility and compassion, while still bringing intensity that pushes teammates and competitors alike to play at a higher level. Love, trust, grit—Phan for Callahan!
